## Root cause identified — hypothesis 1 confirmed, with the exact writer named

The `.git/config` rewrite at 17:36 was performed by a **concurrent Claude Code session (PID 12747, started 17:01:41 PDT)**, via a shell it spawned at **17:36:09 PDT** — matching the recorded `.git/config` mtime to the minute.

### Evidence

`ps -Ao pid,ppid,lstart,command` run 2026-10-27 21:34 PDT shows PID 30648 (parent 12747), started `Tue Oct 27 17:36:09 2026`, running:

```sh
sc=$(ls -d $PWD/.rebar/scratch/df72-*) && \
for r in $(git -C $sc/tracker-copy remote); do git -C $sc/tracker-copy remote remove $r; done
```

`$PWD` was the worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.rebar/worktrees/fix-df72-stale-snapshot-close`, so `$sc` = `.../.rebar/scratch/df72-23558`.

The intent was clearly to strip remotes from a *throwaway copy* of the tracker. It did not do that. `tracker-copy` was produced by a **file copy of the real tracker worktree**, and that copy carried the real worktree's `.git` **file** verbatim:

```
$ cat .../df72-23558/tracker-copy/.git
gitdir: /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker

$ git -C .../df72-23558/tracker-copy rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git
```

That path is **absolute**. A copied worktree is not a copy of a repository — it is a second pointer at the original. So `git -C tracker-copy remote` listed the SHARED repository's remotes (`origin`, `gerrit`), and `git remote remove` wrote to the SHARED `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/config`. That is exactly the observed damage: both `[remote "..."]` sections gone, `[core]`, `[gc]`, `[maintenance]`, `[merge "ours"]`, `[user]`, `[credential]` all intact, because `git remote remove` edits only the sections it owns.

### Status of the three recorded hypotheses

1. **Concurrent session / operator action** — CONFIRMED, with the process, its parent, its start time, and its command line.
2. **A tool that rewrites `.git/config` wholesale** — REFUTED. Nothing rewrote the file wholesale; `git remote remove` surgically deleted two sections, which is why everything else survived. The surgical-survival pattern that looked like "a tool that did not model those sections" is just git's own section editing.
3. **Related to the 18:40 `git timed out after 30s` lock fault** — correlation only, and now explainable: the same runaway process (see below) holds a rebar write lock and runs git operations against the shared object store, so git contention on this host at that time is expected rather than coincidental.

### This is not isolated — the same process also caused bug `painted-epidermal-shelduck` (`f1a2-0755-693d-4924`)

The same shell then ran `converge_snapshot_close_metadata_unit(tracker-copy)` under `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off`. Because `tracker-copy` resolves to the real tracker's git-dir with `HEAD -> refs/heads/tickets`, its REBUILD SNAPSHOT commits landed on the **real local `tickets` branch** and were never pushed. The `tickets` reflog shows exactly 4 such commits (18:56:20, 19:43:57, 20:03:05, 20:53:16) with no intervening `reset: moving to origin/tickets` — which is the 4-ahead/32-behind divergence that ticket reports.

**The process is still running as of 21:35 PDT (elapsed 3h58m)**, with child PID 30670 still executing `run_unit.py`. It belongs to another session; this session has not signalled it. It may make further commits to the shared `tickets` branch.

### What this means for the fix

The AC "identify the writer" is met. The remaining ACs are prevention, and the generalisable defect is now sharper than the original framing: **copying a linked git worktree directory produces a second live handle on the original repository, not an isolated copy.** Any "work on a throwaway copy of the tracker" recipe built with `cp -r` is unsafe by construction — it can rewrite the shared config, move shared refs, and take shared locks. A `make worktree` preflight that names a missing `origin` is still worth having, but it treats the symptom; the durable guard is making the shared checkout's remote configuration recoverable and warning about copied-worktree handles.

Next: proposing the concrete remediation on this ticket before claiming.

## Fix pushed: Gerrit 3252 (commit 215c1ba546e)

**Reproduced first (2026-11-02, sandbox).** In a fresh repo with `origin` and `gerrit`, `cp -R` of a linked worktree followed by `git -C <copy> remote remove <r>` for each remote left `git remote -v` in the main checkout empty: `git -C <copy> rev-parse --git-common-dir` resolved to the main repo's `.git`. Running the repository `Makefile`'s `make worktree` there printed git's raw "'origin' does not appear to be a git repository". This confirms the mechanism recorded in the 2026-10-27 comment.

**Change.**
- `Makefile` `worktree` recipe: `git remote get-url origin` runs before `git fetch`. If `origin` is missing, the recipe prints an `ERROR` naming it, the `git remote add origin https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` command, and the runbook pointer, then exits 1 without fetching. If `gerrit` is missing, it prints a non-fatal `WARNING` that points to the runbook.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`: new section "Restoring the origin and gerrit remotes" with the `origin` URL and both documented `gerrit` forms (HTTPS and SSH), restore commands, and the copied-worktree cause.
- `tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py`: 5 new tests (missing origin stops before fetch with no raw git text; restore command and runbook printed; missing gerrit warns and still succeeds; no warning when both are present; runbook records the URLs).

**Evidence.** The 4 behavior tests were RED against the old recipe (the missing-origin test failed on git's raw message), and all 13 in the file passed after the change. A real-repo sandbox run showed the named ERROR with no remotes, and a warning followed by a normal fetch with only `origin`. `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` clean (753 files), and 750 doc/Makefile-related unit tests passed. `make verify`: the default tier passed (20426 passed, 27 skipped). The integration tier had 1 failure, `test_s3_doctor.py::test_git_remote_s3_api_surface_contract` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'git_remote_s3'`), the known host failure tracked as `dominating-effete-bat`. So the `make verify` AC is not ticked yet.

The general copied-worktree hazard is filed as `asthmatic-grave-caudata` (discovered_from this bug).

## Context / Problem
On 2026-10-27 at about 17:36 PDT both `[remote "origin"]` and `[remote "gerrit"]` sections disappeared from the shared checkout's `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/config`. Every other section survived. After that, `make worktree` (the documented entry point for every change in `AGENTS.md`) and `git push gerrit` both failed. `make worktree` surfaced only git's raw `fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository`, which reads like a network or permissions fault rather than a missing config section.

The writer is identified in the 2026-10-27 comment on this ticket: a concurrent session made a `cp -R` copy of the linked `.tickets-tracker` worktree and ran `git remote remove` for each remote inside the copy. A copied linked worktree keeps the original's `.git` file, so `git -C <copy> rev-parse --git-common-dir` resolves to the real `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git`, and the removal edited the shared config.

Reproduced in a sandbox on 2026-11-02: in a fresh repo with `origin` and `gerrit`, `cp -R` of a linked worktree followed by `git -C <copy> remote remove <r>` for each remote left `git remote -v` in the main checkout empty. Running the repository `Makefile`'s `make worktree name=x` there printed git's raw "does not appear to be a git repository" text before the recipe's generic `'git fetch origin' failed` line.

## Approach
Make the remote configuration recoverable from the tree and make `make worktree` diagnose a missing remote by name, before git's misleading text appears.

1. **Record the canonical URLs in a tracked runbook.** Add a section "Restoring the `origin` and `gerrit` remotes" to `docs/local-dev-env.md`.
   - `origin` has one documented form: `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git`. It is the clone URL in `docs/clone-guidance.md:6`, and `git remote -v` in this host's checkout showed it on 2026-11-02.
   - `gerrit` has two documented forms, and the runbook records both without picking a winner. **HTTPS:** `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/a/rebar`. That is the host and path from the clone command at `CONTRIBUTING.md:63`, and `git remote -v` on this host showed exactly that URL on 2026-11-02, with no embedded username. A contributor may embed `<your-gerrit-username>@` as `CONTRIBUTING.md:63` does. **SSH:** `ssh://<you>@rebar.solutions.navateam.com:29418/rebar`, from `CONTRIBUTING.md:57-58` and `infra/runbooks/github-mirror-lock.md:226`. The runbook tells the reader to restore the form they originally used, because the credentials they set up (HTTP password or SSH key) only work with that scheme.
   - The section gives the exact `git remote add` commands and a check (`git fetch origin`; `git ls-remote gerrit HEAD`). It states that a file copy of a linked worktree shares the original's config, which is how the remotes can disappear (separate bug `asthmatic-grave-caudata`).
2. **Preflight in `make worktree`.** In the `worktree` recipe (`Makefile:227`), before the existing `git fetch origin` step (`Makefile:249-252`), run `git remote get-url origin`. If it fails, print an `ERROR:` line naming the missing `origin` remote, print the `git remote add origin https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` restore command (the only documented `origin` form), point to the new runbook section, and exit non-zero **without** running `git fetch` or `git worktree add`. When `gerrit` is missing, print a non-fatal `WARNING:` naming the missing `gerrit` remote and pointing to the same runbook section for both URL forms, without printing one `gerrit` URL as if it were the only one, then continue, because creating a worktree does not need `gerrit` and only the later push does.
3. **Guard against drift.** A unit test asserts that the `origin` URL the Makefile prints also appears in the runbook section.

Why this fits: the failure happens in the recipe that every change starts with, so the message has to come from there. Putting the URLs in tracked docs means recovery no longer depends on someone's terminal history. Preventing `cp -R` copies of linked worktrees from mutating shared state is a separate, broader defect class. It is filed as its own bug, linked `discovered_from` this one, and is not fixed here.

## Scope
- `Makefile`: `worktree` recipe preflight for `origin` (fatal) and `gerrit` (warning).
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`: new "Restoring the `origin` and `gerrit` remotes" section, with a pointer from the existing "Starting a NEW worktree?" note.
- `tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py`: extend the existing `_GIT_STUB` sandbox so `git remote get-url <name>` can fail for chosen remotes, and add tests.

Out of scope: guarding `cp -R` of linked worktrees (separate bug), and any change to `git` configuration on the host.

## Testing
Extend `tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py`, which already runs the real `Makefile` against a stub `git` on `PATH`. Today `_GIT_STUB` exits 0 for every command other than `fetch` and `worktree add`, so the existing tests keep passing unchanged.
- Missing `origin`: exit is non-zero, combined output has an `ERROR` line naming `origin`, includes `git remote add origin https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` and the runbook pointer, does not include git's "does not appear to be a git repository" text, and the stub log shows no `fetch` and no `worktree add`.
- Missing `gerrit` only: exit 0, `✓ worktree ready` is printed, and a `WARNING` line names `gerrit` and the runbook.
- Both present: the existing happy-path test still passes, and no `WARNING` about remotes is printed.
- Drift: the `origin` URL in the recipe's restore text also appears in `docs/local-dev-env.md`.
Write these tests first and confirm they fail against the current recipe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] The writer of the 17:36 `.git/config` rewrite is identified, or the investigation records exactly which sources were checked and found silent.
  provenance: environment=shared host checkout /Users/joeoakhart/rebar; principal=Rebar Bot Nava agent session; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — writer named from the live process table (ps) in the 2026-10-27 comment, and the mechanism reproduced in a sandbox repo on 2026-11-02 (comment "Fix pushed: Gerrit 3252")
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` records the `origin` URL `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git`; verified by `grep -n "github.com/navapbc/rebar.git" docs/local-dev-env.md`.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` records both documented `gerrit` forms (HTTPS `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/a/rebar` and SSH `ssh://<you>@rebar.solutions.navateam.com:29418/rebar`); verified by `grep -n "rebar.solutions.navateam.com" docs/local-dev-env.md` showing both.
- [x] With `origin` missing, `make worktree` exits non-zero with an `ERROR` line naming `origin` and the runbook section, never running `git fetch`; verified by the new missing-`origin` test in `tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py`.
- [x] With only `gerrit` missing, `make worktree` still succeeds and prints a `WARNING` naming `gerrit`; verified by the new missing-`gerrit` test in `tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py`.
- [x] [non-codebase] `make verify` exits 0 (attested on this ticket: run at 86fa248d9ee, exit 0).
  provenance: environment=local macOS host, worktree fix-sunfish at 86fa248d9ee after make install; principal=Rebar Bot Nava agent session; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — full make verify run exited 0 (20449 passed default tier, 203 passed integration tier), recorded in comment "Landed: Gerrit 3252"
